# Every player can, in theory, become an Antagonist
As long as a player makes sure to make themselves easily detectable, and make it known to the sector that they are Antagonistic, and evil, They can act as antagonists in the meantime, [bold]For example:[/bold]
A group of Cyborgs / AI that have taken over a POI, gotten a ship, and WANT to convert people into more cyborgs, require these things to be made known to the sector, and be able to succesfully be considered "acting antagonist":
- [bold]1: Activity;[/bold] "we are active in the sector", is enough to escalate shortly in shortband in case they want to attack, e.g: "let this be known to the sector, this is OUR, turf, organic, DIE!!", saying "we take place in X, and our ships are Y. we do Z to people, we are gonna kill you." is enough to kill on sight as long as your IFF is on. do not KOS ships or people within 2km of Caelestinius central if you wish to take in antagonistic behaviours.
- [bold]2: Area;[/bold] its better to declare some area as your turf, lets say a 1km No Fly Zone around Tinnia's Rest, "2KM NFZ AROUND TINNIAS REST. ALL WHO TRESPASS THIS AREA WILL BE DEALT WITH HOSTILITY.", this counts as escalation, and anyone who comes into this area is given a short 5 second period to get out of the area, then they can be attacked (communicate this in shortband)
- [bold]3: Severity;[/bold] "We are armed with a Nuclear Fission Device, and are ready to EXPLODE it on ANYONE who does not meet our demands" COULD be proper escalation to KOS, but unless you've given your ship IFF, escalate in shortband before attacking,.
[bold]Example:[/bold]
- [bold]Operator Foxrot (hidden as "Oblique Marrow"):[/bold] "Colonel, you never asked if MY ship was on your side, did you?"
- [bold]Operator Foxrot (no longer hidden):[/bold] "Fool. Take this."
- [bold]4: Objectives;[/bold] to be FULLY antagonist, make sure you have OBJECTIVES, for the AI example i gave before, "KILL, CONSUME, MULTIPLY, CONQUER" COULD pass as objectives, but they are not really creative and instead just engage in the trope of antagonizing for the sake of killing.
